summary: Sicilian Mafia boss Salvatore Lo Piccolo, who had been on the run since 1983 and was considered a successor to Bernardo Provenzano, was arrested at 9:30 a.m. CET in a villa in Giardinello between Cinisi and Terrasini; his son Sandro Lo Piccolo and two other top mafiosi, Gaspare Pulizzi and Andrea Adamo—all four among Italy's top 30 most wanted—were detained. Police fired warning shots as they moved in; the men were armed but did not resist, Sandro cried "I love you dad!" as he was handcuffed, and the four were flown to Palermo's main police station where crowds and anti-Mafia activists gathered during a Palermo day of memory for Mafia victims. After Provenzano's arrest, Lo Piccolo and Matteo Messina Denaro were viewed as potential Cosa Nostra leaders, pizzini found at Provenzano's hide-out named Lo Piccolo and Antonio Rotolo as joint deputies in Palermo, ANSA said Lo Piccolo had the upper hand though Rotolo posed a threat, police uncovered in August a trans-Atlantic alliance and arrested 14 people tied to drug trafficking and money laundering, and Lo Piccolo was reportedly betrayed by lieutenant Francesco Franzese, who was arrested in August and began collaborating with authorities.
